annotations.keyFindings: A three-criterion checklist (specific behaviour, gap, next step) had kappa 0.74 between raters and took about 40 seconds per comment; 35 percent of 600 comments met all three.
annotations.limitations: Three programmes; raters trained by the developers.

annotations.keyFindings: Two prompts in place of one free-text box were followed by comments meeting all criteria rising from 31 to 52 percent, with no fall in forms completed.
annotations.limitations: Uncontrolled before-after comparison; raters not blinded to period.

annotations.keyFindings: Brief workshops raised actionable comments by 14 points at three months against 2 points in a comparison programme, narrowing to 5 points by six months without reminders.
annotations.limitations: Two programmes; allocation not random; attendance 68 percent.

annotations.keyFindings: Residents rated comments with a next step most useful and generic praise least useful; over half rarely read free-text comments.
annotations.limitations: Rating of sample comments, not of their own feedback.

annotations.keyFindings: Women residents were 1.4 times as likely as men to receive comments with no actionable content, after adjustment for year and rotation.
annotations.limitations: Three programmes; gender taken from programme records.

annotations.keyFindings: Monthly individual reports were followed by the median proportion of actionable comments rising from 28 to 47 percent, with a run-chart shift from month five.
annotations.limitations: No comparison group; policy change in month nine.

annotations.keyFindings: Comments on forms completed within 24 hours met all criteria more often than those completed after 48 hours (41 against 19 percent).
annotations.limitations: Association only; batch completion may mark busier rotations.

claims.text: Replacing one free-text box with two feedback prompts was followed by comments meeting all three criteria rising from 31 to 52 percent.
claims.passage: The proportion of comments meeting all three criteria rose from 31 to 52 percent.
claims.interpretation: Supports the form change as a first change idea; the design is uncontrolled.

claims.text: A three-criterion checklist for written comments had substantial agreement between raters and took about 40 seconds per comment.
claims.passage: Agreement was substantial (kappa 0.74), and rating took about 40 seconds per comment.
claims.interpretation: The weekly rating fits the chief residents' protected time.

claims.text: The effect of brief faculty workshops on actionable comments faded by six months without reminders.
claims.passage: By six months, without reminders, the difference had narrowed to 5 points.
claims.interpretation: Micro-teaching needs a reinforcing loop such as individual reports.

claims.text: Women residents were more likely than men to receive written comments with no actionable content.
claims.passage: women were 1.4 times as likely as men to receive a comment with no actionable content
claims.interpretation: Report the outcome by resident gender.

claims.text: Monthly individual reports to faculty were followed by a rise in the median proportion of actionable comments from 28 to 47 percent.
claims.passage: the monthly median proportion of actionable comments rose from 28 to 47 percent
claims.interpretation: Supports individual reports as the reinforcing change; no comparison group.

synthesis: Seven retrieved records, appraised at abstract level. A three-criterion checklist rates comments reliably and quickly. Prompted fields, brief faculty teaching and monthly individual reports were each followed by more actionable comments, but only the teaching study had a comparison group and its effect faded without reminders. Forms completed late carry less specific comments, residents value comments with a next step, and women residents receive non-actionable comments more often. The evidence supports testing a combined package locally with a run chart, balancing measures and a gender breakdown rather than assuming an effect size.
gradeRationale: Mostly uncontrolled single-programme reports with one controlled before-after study; consistent direction but serious risk of bias and fading effects.
summary: Seven retrieved records appraised; five source-derived claims with passages; overall certainty low.
